source.title: Delays in generalization match delayed changes in representational geometry
source.authors: Xingyu Zheng; Kyle Daruwalla; Ari S. Benjamin; D. Klindt

record.tranche_reason: The study tests grokking on image-classification data and argues that changes in the NTK can precede generalization, while representational geometry tracks its onset more closely.
record.gate_note: The study reports delayed generalization under several training setups and measures NTK and representation-geometry changes. Cited results from other papers are not recorded. Figure-only numerical values are not inferred.
record.test_reason: On MNIST and EMNIST image classification, the study induces delayed generalization with weight scaling, weight decay, smaller training sets and output scaling, and removes it with small output scale (V3). It tracks NTK distance and manifold geometry across training, and argues that pre-grokking learning is not lazy, so the lazy-to-rich account needs restating. Neither original source is this study.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors find that in image classification the NTK moves far from initialization before grokking, so pre-grokking learning is not lazy, although a sudden kernel change still accompanies onset. Manifold capacity and geometry stay flat until grokking and change sharply with it, a transition absent without delay. Over-trained non-grokking networks can later lose transferable features. They propose geometry as a better correlate than lazy/rich regimes.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses MNIST and EMNIST image classification with MLPs, AdamW or Adam, and manipulations of weight norm, weight decay, training-set size, or output scaling; it does not reproduce the original small algorithmic-task setup.
record.method_sensitivity: Delayed generalization depends on training setup: the EMNIST model with output scale α = 0.5 shows delay, while α = 0.001 does not. The paper also reports variability across seeds.

fits_no_version.finding: In the non-delayed α=0.001 network, manifold capacity keeps rising late while RM/DM compress. Linear-probe MNIST transfer accuracy drops sharply in late epochs (Fig. 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late over-training can compress representations and lose transferable features even without grokking (feature learning can be lost).

record.problems: Most relevant trajectories are presented in figures without exact numerical values in the text. The authors report variability across seeds in inducing delayed improvement and instability in AdamW training-loss curves.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported result was left out.

untested.parts: No algorithmic datasets. Training size is varied on EMNIST, but no delay lengths versus size are reported.
No circuit identification, Fourier algorithm, or removal of memorizing components.
Text and molecule data not tested; only MLPs on MNIST/EMNIST.
No efficiency account, critical dataset size or ungrokking.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs.
Grokking is also induced with Adam plus weight decay (Appendix Fig. 12), but optimizer or numerical artifacts are not controlled to see whether the delay disappears.

missing.what: Weight norm stays roughly flat, then falls; the caption says the decrease 'precedes improved test performance'. This is a possible anticipating progress measure bearing on V2.
Training-size manipulation (n=1000, 2000, 5000 at fixed weight scaling 10 and decay 0.001) and its grokking trajectories.
missing.versions: V3 (and V1 size-dependence, on non-algorithmic data)

missing.what: Seed variability in inducing delayed generalization.
Grokking also induced with Adam plus weight decay, with a more conventional loss pattern.
Claim that capacity and grokking coincide across all three setups and seeds.

record.verdict_notes: r9 is unlinked from V2 and the record's V2 limits_scope label built on it is dropped. The record's V2 'challenges' label is downgraded to limits_scope: the study shows only that one representational measure fails to anticipate the jump, it identifies no circuit, and its own Appendix Fig. 8 suggests weight norm may precede generalization. Most values are figure-only, and seed variability is acknowledged.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test small algorithmic datasets, chance-to-near-perfect test accuracy on them, or whether smaller training sets take longer to generalize.
It measures representational geometry over training, but does not identify a specific generalizing circuit, test Fourier algorithms, or measure removal of memorizing components.

The study tests image classification and manipulates weight norms, weight decay, and output scaling. It does not test text or molecule data, nor establish that the behavior is generally set by training regime rather than data.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning is studied.
The study does not test an efficient-circuit account, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking below such a size.
The study does not identify or compare learned algorithms across runs.

Although it notes training-loss instability with AdamW and also reports a run with Adam, it does not test whether optimizer or numerical artifacts produce the delay or whether controlling them removes it.

rows.subject: MNIST network
rows.operation_detail: Measured kernel distance during training relative to other training times
rows.value: The kernel changed substantially before grokking.
rows.note: The finding qualifies a lazy-to-rich account in which the network would remain near its initial kernel until delayed generalization.
rows.check: Bears on V3's lazy-to-rich characterization. The kernel moves far from initialization before grokking, contrary to a lazy phase. Authors still report a sudden kernel change at onset. Block-structured kernel changes also occur in non-grokked networks, so this is not a V2 progress measure.
